name: aegisdb-surface
description: The wire surface of this project as typed facts: the operations, the retrieval modes, the flags and request parameters, and what each one defaults to or is disabled by. Written in the same ten predicates as predicates.example.json, and deliberately sharing entity prose with tools/facts/aegisdb.json so both corpora bind to the same records — that corpus says what the server is made of, this one says what it exposes.

entities.op_tokens: the token_list, token_add and token_revoke operations

facts: A read operation is a wire operation.
A write operation is a wire operation.
An admin-only operation is a wire operation.
A maintenance sweep is a write operation: it tombstones records.
The wire operations are dispatched by the query layer's router.
A retrieval mode is one of the ways search selects and ranks candidates.
ping is a read operation, and the one op always exempt from authentication.
get fetches one record by id without incrementing its recall counters.
search is the unified read: time, tags, vector, text, and typed-fact filters, all combinable.
count answers how many records match the filters without returning them.
history returns the version trail of one record.
traverse walks the relationship graph breadth-first.
export pages one subject's records out of the store.
conflicts lists contradiction pairs and resolves none of them.
predicates reports the vocabulary a fact may be written in.
insert appends a record, or a batch of up to 1000, to the log.
update appends a new version of a semantic record.
delete tombstones a record by id, or every record matching a filter.
relate records a directed edge between two persisted records.
promote copies a working-memory entry into the persistent log.
purge hard-deletes a namespace and compacts the payloads off disk.
consolidate merges near-duplicate semantic memories mechanically.
forget tombstones aging, low-value records so the corpus plateaus.
stats is admin-only; a namespaced token receives FORBIDDEN.
snapshot takes a consistent online backup and is admin-only.
The token management ops change accepted tokens at runtime and are admin-only.

Lexical BM25 search ranks records by the words their payload contains.
Semantic search ranks by cosine similarity weighted by importance x confidence.
Hybrid search fuses the lexical and semantic lists by reciprocal rank.
Pattern search filters on the typed fact a record asserts rather than on its words.
Subsumption expands a bound pattern subject over the is_a taxonomy.
Reverse traversal follows relationships backwards, from target to source.
Reverse traversal is the direction:in half of the traverse operation.
Lexical search reads the BM25 postings.
Semantic search reads the HNSW graph once the corpus passes the ANN threshold.
Hybrid search needs the lexical list to fuse.
Hybrid search needs the semantic list to fuse.
Pattern lookups are answered by the fact indexes.
Subsumption reads the is_a closure the inference job materializes.
Subsumption expands a pattern, so it needs the fact indexes too.
A backward walk needs the reverse edge index; a record lists only the edges it points along.
forget weighs recall history, which only the usage index records.
The conflicts list is the set the inference pass fills as it counts.
Without the inference job nothing has scanned, so conflicts answers empty.
history reconstructs versions from the on-disk log.
A snapshot is the log's durable prefix plus fresh metadata.
purge needs compaction to make the payloads actually leave disk.
promote takes a working-memory entry as its input.
The predicates op reports what the registry declares.
The inference job draws only what the registry declares.
Recovery rebuilds every record-describing index from the log.
Recovery trusts the checkpoint's covered prefix and scans only the tail.
The predicate registry is the query layer's write-path contract for facts.
The index checkpoint is written beside the log.
Recovery is the storage layer's startup path.
Token authentication is resolved before dispatch.
Phase gating caps which operations the router will dispatch.
Encryption at rest changes the frame layout of the log and the checkpoints.
The record model is what the log encodes and the indexes describe.
Episodic memory is immutable: update on an episodic id returns IMMUTABLE.
Semantic memory is mutable: update appends a new version and the latest wins.
Working memory is a volatile per-session ring buffer, never written to the log until promoted.
Episodic is one of the three record types.
Semantic is one of the three record types.
Working is one of the three record types.
Pattern search returns NOT_READY when the fact indexes are off.
A query search returns NOT_READY when the lexical index is off.
direction:in and direction:both return NOT_READY without the reverse edge index.
subsume returns NOT_READY unless the inference job is running.
Without --inference the conflicts list is empty rather than absent.
The registry is loaded, and enforced, only when this names a file.
Authentication is off until tokens are configured.
Encryption at rest is enabled per data directory by the key file.
A server becomes a follower only when pointed at a primary.
The phase flag caps the highest enabled feature tier.
Setting it to 0 disables checkpointing, so recovery scans the whole log.
--embedding-dim fixes the vector length every client must match.
--phase caps the highest enabled feature tier.
--durability chooses sync, batch, or interval fsync.
--fsync-interval-ms is the interval mode's flush period.
--fsync-batch is the batch mode's record count.
--checkpoint-sec is how often the index checkpoint is refreshed.
--compact-sec is how often the maintenance thread compacts.
--working-capacity sizes the per-session working ring buffer.
--query-scan-cap bounds a broad, filterless search or count.
--max-payload is the point at which a record body is PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE.
--io-threads sets the number of poll() event loops, not the connection cap.
--idle-timeout-sec closes a connection making no byte progress.
--max-connections is a hard cap on concurrent client connections.
--max-index-bytes is the in-RAM index ceiling that makes an insert MEMORY_LIMIT.
--inference-max-derived bounds the records one pass writes.
--inference-max-subsume bounds how far a subsumption expansion reaches.
A vector of any other length is INVALID_REQUEST.
Everything is enabled by default; most deployments never set it.
Loss is bounded by time rather than by write count.
